Review the game specification at docs/2d-browser-runner-spec.md against the original brief docs/2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md. This is a READ-ONLY review — do NOT edit any files; return your findings as your output.

Context: the spec was written from a user interview that made these deliberate choices — finite level (not endless), MVP = 1 hero dog (5-breed select deferred to phase 2), controls = tap-jump only (duck/slide + combo deferred), Armor power-up + sound IN, CTA = single promo-code path to tabletki.ua only (no client-site path in MVP), stack = Phaser 3 + TS + Vite, static hosting, analytics via a track() adapter to GA4 + Meta Pixel. These deferrals are INTENTIONAL — do NOT flag a consciously-deferred item as 'missing'; only flag it if the spec fails to acknowledge the deferral or the roadmap is unclear.

Check for:
1. COMPLETENESS — does the spec cover every brief must-have, either in MVP or as an explicitly-noted phase-2 item? List anything from the brief that is neither covered nor consciously deferred.
2. CONSISTENCY — internal contradictions (e.g. a mechanic described one way in gameplay and another in the flow/HUD), or anything that contradicts the locked decisions above.
3. ANALYTICS CONTRACT — are start_game / finish_game / click_buy each specified with clear fire-points and a sound param set? Any gap that would make GA4 / Meta Pixel wiring ambiguous?
4. TECH SOUNDNESS — is the Phaser 3 + TS + Vite architecture / scene breakdown / asset pipeline coherent and buildable for this scope? Any red flags?
5. RISKS / GAPS — anything under-specified that would bite during implementation or estimation (iOS audio unlock, perf budget, asset counts, open client questions).

Return a concise findings list. For each finding give: severity (blocker / major / minor / nit), the section, a one-line description, and a suggested fix. If the spec is solid, say so and keep the list short. End with a one-line overall verdict (ship-ready / minor fixes / needs work).

I've read both documents. This is a focused doc-vs-doc review — no further research needed. Here are my findings.

## Spec review: `2d-browser-runner-spec.md` vs. `2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md`

**Completeness (check 1):** Every brief must-have is either in MVP or explicitly deferred. The five locked decisions (finite level, 1 dog, jump-only, Armor+sound IN, single tabletki.ua CTA, Phaser+TS+Vite, static, `track()` adapter) are all faithfully reflected and correctly traced back to the brief. No genuinely missing must-haves.

**Consistency (check 2):** Internally coherent — HP=3, 60–90s, jump-only, one dog, single CTA, Armor-exception all stated consistently across gameplay/flow/HUD/scenes. No contradictions found.

**Analytics contract (check 3):** All three events have clear fire-points and parameter tables. Solid — the gaps below are clarifications, not missing wiring.

**Tech soundness (check 4):** Phaser 3 + TS + Vite, scene breakdown, atlas/audio pipeline, pooling, static deploy — coherent and buildable for this scope. No red flags, just two under-specifications.

### Findings

| # | Sev | Section | Finding | Suggested fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **minor** | §7.2 vs §6.3 | `duration_s` is defined as "wall-clock," but pause *freezes the game clock*. Real wall-clock would include paused time and inflate the metric; analysts almost certainly want play-time. | State explicitly that `duration_s` excludes pause (recommended) and how the timer is measured. |
| 2 | **minor** | §7.3 | GA4 custom params (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`, `destination`, `promo_code`) will be collected but **won't appear in GA4 reports unless registered as custom dimensions/metrics** in the property. Not mentioned. | Add a one-line note that these params must be registered in GA4 Admin for reporting. |
| 3 | **minor** | §6.4 / §7.2 | **No UTM/campaign params on the tabletki.ua URL.** The intent KPI (`click_buy/start_game`) is fine client-side, but with a single static promo code (§11 Q3) and a bare link, the client can't attribute *purchases completed on tabletki.ua* back to the campaign. | Append UTM params to the buy URL (or explicitly mark purchase-side attribution out of scope). |
| 4 | **minor** | §3.9 / §8.2 | **Level termination under-specified.** "Finite level + finish line" is stated, but neither the length unit (distance vs time) nor how/when the finish line spawns is defined; §8.2 has no `FinishLine` entity. | Specify level length (px or duration) and finish-line spawn rule; optionally add `FinishLine` to the structure. |
| 5 | **nit** | §3.3 vs brief §3 | Brief says ticks "Remove health / deduct points"; spec uses **HP-only** damage with no acknowledgment that the points-deduction reading was dropped. | One line noting points-deduction was intentionally replaced by HP-only. |
| 6 | **nit** | §8.2 / §8.3 | Physics engine and Phaser Scale mode are never named (Arcade + FIT are the obvious defaults but unstated). | State Phaser Arcade Physics + a named Scale mode. |
| 7 | **nit** | §4.2 vs brief §3A | Brief offered park/forest/city avenue; spec commits to **park only** but doesn't list the theme in §11 client confirmations. | Add theme choice to §11. |

### Verdict

**Minor fixes.** The spec is ship-ready as an estimate/baseline — thorough, internally consistent, and faithful to every locked decision. The only items with real teeth are the three analytics-clarity gaps (1–3: pause-aware `duration_s`, GA4 custom-dimension registration, UTM attribution), all cheap to address.

Now I'll mark this node ready for the orchestrator.

1	# Game Specification — 2D Browser Runner (Working title: *Happy Dog Runner*)
2	
3	**Document type:** Product & technical specification (buildable scope for estimate)
4	**Status:** Draft for client confirmation
5	**Source of requirements:** [`docs/2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md`](./2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md) (client cost-estimation brief, English translation)
6	**Date:** 2026-07-23
7	
8	> **How to read this document.** The client brief is the source of *requirements*. A product interview then locked a set of *decisions* that resolve the brief's open ambiguities (e.g. endless vs. finite, MVP vs. phase 2). Where a locked decision narrows or overrides the brief, this spec follows the decision and says so. Section 11 lists what still needs client confirmation before a firm cost/timeline can be committed.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Overview & Goals
13	
14	### 1.1 What we are building
15	
16	A **mobile-first, branded 2D browser runner** that promotes a dog flea-and-tick tablet. The player controls a hero dog that auto-runs through a park, jumps over obstacles, avoids **ticks**, and collects **tablets**. The round is a **finite single level (~60–90 s)** ending in **Victory** (reach the finish line) or **Game Over** (lose all health). After the round, a single call-to-action surfaces a **promo code** and links to **[tabletki.ua](http://tabletki.ua)** to buy the product.
17	
18	This is an advergame: the gameplay is the vehicle, and the marketing outcomes are the point.
19	
20	### 1.2 Marketing objective
21	
22	Per the brief (§1), two goals:
23	
24	1. **Awareness** — teach, through play, that ticks are a threat and the tablet is the protection. The "tablet as armor" power-up (§3.7) makes the product mechanic *be* the protection.
25	2. **Conversion** — drive tablet purchase via the post-round CTA to tabletki.ua (brief §3, "CTA button").
26	
27	### 1.3 Audience
28	
29	Dog owners on **mobile web**, reached through paid social / display where Meta Pixel and GA4 attribution matter. Casual players; sessions are short and one-handed. UI language assumed **Ukrainian primary**, built i18n-ready (see §11).
30	
31	### 1.4 Success signals (tied to the three analytics events)
32	
33	The entire funnel is observable through three events (full contract in §7):
34	
35	| Funnel stage | Signal | Event |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Engagement | Player starts a round | `start_game` |
38	| Completion & quality | Player finishes (win or lose), with score & duration | `finish_game` (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`) |
39	| **Conversion** | Player taps the buy CTA | `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) |
40	
41	Primary KPI is `click_buy / start_game` (intent-to-purchase rate). `finish_game` with `result=win` vs. `lose` and `duration_s` tells us whether difficulty is tuned so players actually reach the CTA.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 2. Platforms & Performance Targets
46	
47	### 2.1 Platform priority
48	
49	**Mobile web first**, desktop supported (brief §2). Touch is the primary input; desktop uses tap/click and spacebar.
50	
51	### 2.2 Supported browser matrix
52	
53	| Tier | Browser / OS | Support level |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| Primary | iOS Safari (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
56	| Primary | Android Chrome (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
57	| Secondary | Desktop Chrome / Edge / Firefox (current) | Fully supported |
58	| Secondary | Desktop Safari (current) | Fully supported |
59	| Best-effort | Samsung Internet, mobile Firefox | Should work; not a QA gate |
60	
61	### 2.3 Performance budget (assumed — **flag for confirmation**, see §11)
62	
63	Because the brief sets no numbers, we propose these targets. They drive art budgets and QA gates and must be confirmed:
64	
65	| Metric | Target | Notes |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Frame rate | 60 FPS on mid-range phones; **≥30 FPS floor** on low-end (≈2–3-year-old Android) | Gameplay must never dip below the floor |
68	| Time-to-interactive (first load, warm CDN) | **≤3 s** on a 4G connection | Menu interactive |
69	| Initial download (gzipped) | **≤4–6 MB** total (code + assets) | Aggressive for an advergame; see §10.5 |
70	| Input latency (tap → jump) | ≤1 frame of processing | Tap responsiveness is the whole game |
71	| Orientation | Portrait-first; graceful landscape | Confirm preferred orientation |
72	
73	These are the recommended KPIs to lock in §11.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 3. Gameplay Design
78	
79	### 3.1 Core loop
80	
81	```
82	auto-run forward  →  read upcoming hazard  →  tap to jump  →  land / collect / take hit
83	      ↑                                                                    │
84	      └──────────────────── repeat until finish line or 0 HP ──────────────┘
85	```
86	
87	The player does exactly one thing — **time jumps** — against a scrolling stream of obstacles, ticks, and tablets. Skill = timing and reading density as speed ramps.
88	
89	### 3.2 Controls (locked)
90	
91	**Auto-run + tap-to-jump ONLY.** No duck/slide, no lane-switching in MVP.
92	
93	| Input | Platform | Action |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| Tap anywhere on canvas | Mobile | Jump |
96	| Spacebar / click | Desktop | Jump |
97	| Pause button (HUD) | All | Pause / resume |
98	| Mute button (HUD) | All | Toggle audio |
99	
100	- Single jump (no double-jump in MVP). Jump arc is fixed height/duration, tuned so a well-timed tap clears one obstacle.
101	- Jump is **edge-triggered** (fires on press, not hold) and ignored while airborne.
102	
103	> Duck/slide is explicitly **deferred to phase 2** (§9). Spec'd here as absent so level design assumes a jump-only vocabulary.
104	
105	### 3.3 Entities
106	
107	| Entity | Role | Behavior |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **Hero dog** | Player avatar | Auto-runs; fixed screen X; jumps on input; has HP |
110	| **Tick** | Damaging obstacle / enemy | Ground or low-flying hazard; collision = **−1 HP**. The thing you must avoid |
111	| **Environmental obstacle** (bush / puddle) | Jump obstacle | Per brief §3A; collision = **−1 HP** (treated as a hazard you jump). *Assumption: same damage model as tick; confirm if bush/puddle should be harmless-but-blocking instead* (§11) |
112	| **Tablet** | Collectible (the product) | Pickup = **+score** and **+1 HP** up to the 3-heart cap |
113	| **Armor / shield pickup** | Timed power-up | Pickup = temporary invulnerability (see §3.7) |
114	| **Finish line** | Level end | Reaching it = Victory |
115	
116	### 3.4 Health rules (locked)
117	
118	- Player starts with **3 HP**, shown as 3 hearts.
119	- **Tick collision: −1 HP.** Environmental-obstacle collision: −1 HP (see assumption above).
120	- **Tablet pickup: +1 HP**, capped at 3 (never exceeds the 3-heart max).
121	- **0 HP → Game Over.**
122	- On taking damage: brief invulnerability/blink window (~1 s) + hit animation, so a single obstacle can't drain multiple hearts in one contact.
123	
124	### 3.5 Scoring (locked direction)
125	
126	- **Tablets collected → +score** (primary source; ties score to the product).
127	- **Distance / survival → +score** over time (secondary, keeps score moving).
128	- Score is displayed live in the HUD and reported in `finish_game` (§7).
129	- **Combo / score-multiplier is deferred to phase 2** (§9). MVP score is a straight sum.
130	
131	*Exact point values (e.g. tablet = 100, per-second = 10) are tuning parameters, set during playtest.*
132	
133	### 3.6 Win / lose conditions (locked)
134	
135	| Outcome | Trigger | Result screen | Analytics |
136	|---|---|---|---|
137	| **Victory** | Reach the finish line with ≥1 HP | Victory screen | `finish_game` `result:'win'` |
138	| **Game Over** | HP reaches 0 before finish | Game Over screen | `finish_game` `result:'lose'` |
139	
140	Both screens surface the same buy CTA (§6.4).
141	
142	### 3.7 Armor power-up (locked — optional feature IN MVP)
143	
144	Per brief §3 ("medication as Armor", Crash-Bandicoot-mask principle):
145	
146	- A distinct **Armor/shield pickup** appears occasionally in the level.
147	- On pickup: hero gains **temporary total invulnerability** — tick/obstacle collisions do **no damage** for the duration.
148	- **Distinct visual:** a shield aura / mask-style overlay on the dog (brief's Crash-Bandicoot mask reference), plus a countdown/expiry tell (aura flashes as it runs out).
149	- Duration is a tuning parameter (proposed **~4–6 s**).
150	- While armored, hitting a tick still consumes/destroys the tick (feels powerful) but costs no HP.
151	- Reinforces the marketing message: *the tablet is the protection.*
152	
153	### 3.8 Difficulty progression (locked)
154	
155	The level ramps over its ~60–90 s so the finish feels earned:
156	
157	- **Scroll speed** increases in stages from start to finish.
158	- **Obstacle & tick density** increases (tighter spacing, more frequent hazards).
159	- **Tablet/armor generosity** tapers slightly late-game to raise tension near the finish.
160	- Ramp is authored/curve-driven (not purely random) so difficulty is repeatable and tunable. Spacing always stays clearable with jump-only controls (§3.2).
161	
162	### 3.9 Session length (locked)
163	
164	**One finite level, ~60–90 s.** Not endless. A defined finish line exists. This keeps sessions short, guarantees most players reach a result screen (and thus the CTA), and bounds art/level-authoring scope.
165	
166	---
167	
168	## 4. Content & Art Requirements
169	
170	> Per brief §3A, the estimate must separate **Code** from **Design/Animation**. This section is the Design/Animation manifest. Art style: **cartoon/casual mobile**, single **park** theme.
171	
172	### 4.1 Hero dog — 5 animation states (brief §3A)
173	
174	**MVP ships ONE hero dog** (breed selection deferred, §9). That one dog needs all five states:
175	
176	| # | Animation | Trigger |
177	|---|---|---|
178	| 1 | **Run** | Default auto-run loop |
179	| 2 | **Jump** | On tap (rise + fall; can be one clip or 2-part) |
180	| 3 | **Damage / hit** | On taking −1 HP |
181	| 4 | **Victory** | Victory screen / crossing finish |
182	| 5 | **Defeat** | Game Over |
183	
184	Delivered as a **spritesheet/texture atlas** with frame data (see §8.4). *(Bonus "armored run" tint/overlay can be a shader/tint on the run loop rather than a separate sheet — cost-saving.)*
185	
186	### 4.2 Environment — park (brief §3A)
187	
188	- Single **park** theme.
189	- **1–2 parallax background layers** (e.g. far skyline/treeline + near foliage) scrolling at different speeds for depth.
190	- Repeating ground/path tile.
191	- Optional light foreground layer (grass tufts) if budget allows.
192	
193	### 4.3 Enemies, collectibles, obstacles
194	
195	| Asset | Count | Notes |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| **Tick** | 1 type | Idle/approach animation (small loop or single frame with wobble) |
198	| **Tablet** (brand product) | 1 type | Should read as the actual product; gentle spin/shine loop |
199	| **Environmental obstacles** | 1–2 types | Bush and/or puddle (brief §3A) |
200	| **Armor / shield pickup** | 1 | Distinct mask/shield icon; pickup burst VFX |
201	
202	### 4.4 Armor VFX
203	
204	- Pickup burst (on collect).
205	- Active-shield aura/overlay on the dog (persistent during duration).
206	- Expiry tell (flash/fade in final ~1 s).
207	
208	### 4.5 UI screens (art) — brief §3A UI/UX
209	
210	- **Main menu** (title, Play, mute, branding).
211	- **HUD** (score, hearts, progress/timer, pause, mute).
212	- **Victory** results screen (score + CTA).
213	- **Game Over** results screen (score + CTA).
214	- **Pause** overlay.
215	- Shared UI kit: buttons, hearts (full/empty), promo-code chip, iconography.
216	
217	> The brief lists a **dog-selection screen** under UI. Because breed select is **deferred to phase 2**, that screen is **not** an MVP art deliverable (roadmap only, §9).
218	
219	### 4.6 Audio asset list (locked — sound IN MVP)
220	
221	| Asset | Type | Use |
222	|---|---|---|
223	| Jump SFX | one-shot | On jump |
224	| Hit SFX | one-shot | On −1 HP |
225	| Pickup SFX | one-shot | On tablet/armor collect |
226	| Victory sting | short | Victory screen |
227	| Game Over sting | short | Game Over screen |
228	| Music loop | short seamless loop | Background during play |
229	| (Mute state) | — | Handled in code (§6.3), persists across screens |
230	
231	Audio must respect the **iOS Safari audio-unlock** requirement (§10.2).
232	
233	---
234	
235	## 5. Screen Flow & State Machine
236	
237	### 5.1 Flow
238	
239	```mermaid
240	stateDiagram-v2
241	    [*] --> Boot
242	    Boot --> Preload
243	    Preload --> Menu
244	    Menu --> Play: tap Play  //  fires start_game
245	    Play --> Victory: reach finish (HP>0)  //  fires finish_game(result=win)
246	    Play --> GameOver: HP == 0  //  fires finish_game(result=lose)
247	    Play --> Play: Pause/Resume
248	    Victory --> Buy: tap CTA  //  fires click_buy
249	    GameOver --> Buy: tap CTA  //  fires click_buy
250	    Victory --> Play: Play again
251	    GameOver --> Play: Play again
252	    Buy --> [*]: leave to tabletki.ua
253	```
254	
255	### 5.2 Where each analytics event fires
256	
257	| Transition | Event | Notes |
258	|---|---|---|
259	| Menu → Play (round begins) | **`start_game`** | Fired once as the Play scene starts the run |
260	| Play → Victory | **`finish_game`** `result:'win'` | With `score`, `duration_s` |
261	| Play → Game Over | **`finish_game`** `result:'lose'` | With `score`, `duration_s` |
262	| Results → tap CTA | **`click_buy`** | With `destination`, `promo_code`; then navigate to tabletki.ua |
263	
264	"Play again" re-enters Play and fires a fresh `start_game`.
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 6. UI / HUD Spec
269	
270	### 6.1 Main menu
271	
272	- Game title + branding (logo — see §11).
273	- **Play** button (primary).
274	- Mute toggle.
275	- Optional: short "how to play" hint ("Tap to jump — dodge the ticks!").
276	- (Phase 2: breed-select entry point — hidden in MVP.)
277	
278	### 6.2 In-game HUD (brief §3A: score, HP, timer/progress)
279	
280	Persistent, minimal, thumb-safe:
281	
282	| Element | Position (proposed) | Content |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| **Score** | Top-left | Live numeric score |
285	| **HP hearts** | Top-center or top-left under score | 3 hearts, filled/empty |
286	| **Level progress** | Top, full-width thin bar **or** countdown timer | Distance-to-finish (progress bar preferred; shows the finish is coming) |
287	| **Pause** | Top-right | Opens pause overlay |
288	| **Mute** | Top-right (next to pause) | Toggles audio |
289	
290	Progress bar preferred over a raw timer because it visualizes "the finish line is near," which encourages completion (and CTA exposure).
291	
292	### 6.3 Pause & mute
293	
294	- **Pause overlay:** dims play, shows Resume + Mute + (optional) Quit-to-menu. Game clock and scrolling freeze.
295	- **Mute:** toggles all audio; state **persisted** (localStorage) across scenes and sessions. Reflected by icon in menu, HUD, and pause.
296	
297	### 6.4 Results screens (Victory & Game Over) — the CTA
298	
299	Both screens share a layout; only framing/art differ:
300	
301	| Element | Victory | Game Over |
302	|---|---|---|
303	| Headline | "You made it! 🐕" | "Ticks got you…" |
304	| Final score | shown | shown |
305	| Result art | Victory dog pose | Defeat dog pose |
306	| **Buy CTA (single)** | Promo code + "Buy on tabletki.ua" | same |
307	| Secondary | "Play again" | "Play again" |
308	
309	**CTA (the `click_buy` conversion, locked):**
310	- **One** primary call-to-action on the results screen.
311	- Displays a **promo code** (copyable) and a button linking to **tabletki.ua**.
312	- On tap: fire `click_buy` (`destination:'tabletki.ua'`, `promo_code`) **then** navigate (new tab on desktop; confirm same-tab vs new-tab behavior for mobile in §11).
313	- **No client-site path in MVP** — tabletki.ua only.
314	
315	---
316	
317	## 7. Analytics & Tracking Spec
318	
319	### 7.1 Adapter design
320	
321	A **thin `track(event, params)` adapter** is the single choke point for all analytics. Game code never calls `gtag`/`fbq` directly — it calls `track()`, which fans out to **GA4 (gtag)** and **Meta Pixel (fbq)**.
322	
323	```ts
324	type AnalyticsEvent = 'start_game' | 'finish_game' | 'click_buy';
325	
326	function track(event: AnalyticsEvent, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
327	  // GA4
328	  window.gtag?.('event', event, params);
329	  // Meta Pixel — custom events via trackCustom
330	  window.fbq?.('trackCustom', event, params);
331	  // Dev/QA: console mirror when a debug flag is on
332	  if (DEBUG_ANALYTICS) console.debug('[track]', event, params);
333	}
334	```
335	
336	Rationale:
337	- **One contract, two sinks.** Adding/removing a sink (or a consent gate) is a one-file change.
338	- **Safe if a pixel is absent.** Optional chaining means a missing/blocked `gtag`/`fbq` never throws (ad-blockers are common on the audience).
339	- **Testable.** Event emission can be asserted in isolation.
340	
341	### 7.2 Event / parameter contract
342	
343	#### `start_game` — a round begins
344	
345	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
346	|---|---|---|---|---|
347	| *(none required)* | — | — | — | Fired once when the Play scene starts the run |
348	
349	#### `finish_game` — fires on BOTH Victory and Game Over
350	
351	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
352	|---|---|---|---|---|
353	| `result` | `'win' \| 'lose'` | ✅ | `'win'` | `win` = reached finish; `lose` = 0 HP |
354	| `score` | integer | ✅ | `1450` | Final score at round end |
355	| `duration_s` | integer (seconds) | ✅ | `72` | Wall-clock round length, start → end |
356	
357	#### `click_buy` — CTA tapped on results screen
358	
359	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
360	|---|---|---|---|---|
361	| `destination` | string | ✅ | `'tabletki.ua'` | Fixed for MVP |
362	| `promo_code` | string | ✅ | `'DOG10'` | The code shown on the CTA (see §11) |
363	
364	> All three event **names** are fixed by the brief (§3B: `start_game`, `finish_game`, `click_buy`) — do not rename.
365	
366	### 7.3 GA4 (gtag) + Meta Pixel (fbq) wiring
367	
368	- Both snippets load in `index.html` `<head>` (standard install), parameterized by **GA4 Measurement ID** and **Meta Pixel ID** (see §11 — needed before launch).
369	- IDs injected via Vite env vars (`VITE_GA4_ID`, `VITE_FB_PIXEL_ID`) so staging/prod differ without code edits.
370	- GA4 receives events via `gtag('event', …)`; Meta Pixel via `fbq('trackCustom', …)`. (Meta standard events like `Purchase` are **not** used — the brief's three custom names take priority; a `Purchase` mapping can be added later if the client wants Ads Manager optimization on it.)
371	
372	### 7.4 Consent / GDPR note
373	
374	- The audience is EU-adjacent (Ukraine); ad pixels imply personal-data processing.
375	- **Recommendation:** a lightweight consent gate. `track()` is the natural enforcement point — buffer or drop events until consent is granted, and only initialize `fbq`/`gtag` post-consent (Consent Mode v2 for GA4).
376	- Exact consent UX / whether a CMP is required depends on the client's legal stance — **flag in §11.** MVP ships the adapter consent-ready even if the banner is deferred.
377	
378	---
379	
380	## 8. Technical Architecture
381	
382	### 8.1 Stack (locked)
383	
384	**Phaser 3 + TypeScript + Vite**, shipped as a **100% static site** (Cloudflare Pages or Netlify). **No backend/server.** (Brief §3B leaves engine to us and asks for "something simple"; Phaser 3 is the standard, well-supported HTML5 2D choice.)
385	
386	### 8.2 Proposed project structure
387	
388	```
389	/
390	├─ index.html                # GA4 + Meta Pixel snippets, canvas mount
391	├─ vite.config.ts
392	├─ public/
393	│  └─ assets/                # atlases, audio, fonts (hashed on build)
394	├─ src/
395	│  ├─ main.ts                # Phaser.Game bootstrap + config
396	│  ├─ scenes/
397	│  │  ├─ BootScene.ts        # config, scale mode, input setup
398	│  │  ├─ PreloadScene.ts     # load atlases/audio + loading bar
399	│  │  ├─ MenuScene.ts        # main menu (fires nothing)
400	│  │  ├─ GameScene.ts        # the run: spawn, collide, HP, score
401	│  │  └─ ResultsScene.ts     # Victory/Game Over + CTA (win/lose param)
402	│  ├─ entities/
403	│  │  ├─ HeroDog.ts          # run/jump/hit/win/lose states + HP
404	│  │  ├─ Tick.ts
405	│  │  ├─ Tablet.ts
406	│  │  ├─ Obstacle.ts         # bush/puddle
407	│  │  └─ ArmorPickup.ts
408	│  ├─ systems/
409	│  │  ├─ Spawner.ts          # difficulty-curve-driven spawning
410	│  │  ├─ DifficultyCurve.ts  # speed/density ramp over the level
411	│  │  └─ AudioManager.ts     # SFX/music + mute persistence + iOS unlock
412	│  ├─ analytics/
413	│  │  └─ track.ts            # the track() adapter (§7)
414	│  ├─ ui/
415	│  │  ├─ Hud.ts              # score, hearts, progress, pause, mute
416	│  │  └─ PauseOverlay.ts
417	│  ├─ config/
418	│  │  ├─ gameConfig.ts       # HP, jump, speeds, durations (tuning)
419	│  │  └─ env.ts              # VITE_* ids, promo code, buy URL
420	│  └─ i18n/
421	│     └─ strings.ts          # UA strings, i18n-ready (§11)
422	```
423	
424	### 8.3 Phaser Scene breakdown
425	
426	| Scene | Responsibility | Analytics |
427	|---|---|---|
428	| **Boot** | Game config, scale/resize mode, input, load minimal boot assets | — |
429	| **Preload** | Load all atlases/audio; show loading bar; wire iOS audio-unlock | — |
430	| **Menu** | Title, Play, mute | — |
431	| **Game** | The run — spawner, collisions, HP, score, HUD, pause, armor | fires `start_game` on start; `finish_game` on end |
432	| **Results** | Victory/Game Over by param; score; promo CTA; Play again | fires `click_buy` on CTA |
433	
434	### 8.4 Asset pipeline
435	
436	- **Spritesheets → texture atlases** (packed `.png` + JSON frame data) for the dog and entities — one atlas draw call, fewer requests, good mobile GPU behavior.
437	- Audio as compressed `.m4a`/`.mp3` (+ `.ogg` fallback where useful); short loops.
438	- Vite **content-hashes** asset filenames for cache-busting; static host serves with long cache TTLs.
439	- Textures loaded in Preload with a visible loading bar.
440	
441	### 8.5 Build & deployment
442	
443	- `vite build` → static `dist/` (HTML, hashed JS/CSS, assets).
444	- Deploy `dist/` to **Cloudflare Pages or Netlify** — global CDN, no server.
445	- Env-specific IDs (GA4, Pixel, promo code, buy URL) via `VITE_*` build env vars.
446	- CI: build on push, deploy preview per branch, promote to prod.
447	
448	---
449	
450	## 9. Scope & Phasing
451	
452	### 9.1 MVP (this spec)
453	
454	- One finite park level (~60–90 s) with finish line.
455	- **One** hero dog with 5 animations (run/jump/hit/victory/defeat).
456	- Auto-run + tap-to-jump.
457	- 3 HP; tick/obstacle damage; tablet pickup (+score, +HP capped at 3).
458	- Ticks, bush/puddle obstacles, tablet collectibles.
459	- **Armor/shield** power-up (timed invulnerability, distinct VFX).
460	- Difficulty ramp (speed + density).
461	- **Sound** (SFX, music loop, mute toggle, iOS audio-unlock).
462	- Menu, HUD, Pause, Victory & Game Over screens.
463	- Single promo-code CTA to tabletki.ua.
464	- `track()` adapter → GA4 + Meta Pixel with the 3 events.
465	- Static deployment.
466	
467	### 9.2 Phase-2 roadmap (deferred — spec'd, not built now)
468	
469	| Deferred feature | Why deferred | What phase 2 adds |
470	|---|---|---|
471	| **5-breed character selection** | Brief lists 5 skins + a select screen; MVP proves the loop with one dog to control art cost & scope. **Whether this is committed is an open question (§11).** | 4 more dog atlases (×5 animations each) + dog-selection screen + persistence of choice |
472	| **Duck / slide mechanic** | Jump-only keeps controls and level-authoring simple for MVP and mobile ergonomics | Second input verb + low/overhead obstacles designed around it |
473	| **Combo / score-multiplier** | MVP scoring is a straight sum; multiplier is a retention/polish layer, not core | Combo tracking on tablet streaks, multiplier UI, juicier feedback |
474	
475	Deferrals are deliberate scope control, not omissions — each is a clean additive increment on the MVP architecture (the entity/scene structure in §8 already accommodates them).
476	
477	---
478	
479	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
480	
481	### 10.1 Performance
482	
483	- Meet the budget in §2.3 (confirm targets). 60 FPS mid-range, ≥30 FPS floor low-end.
484	- Object pooling for spawned entities (ticks, tablets, obstacles) — no per-spawn GC churn.
485	- Atlas-based rendering to minimize draw calls.
486	
487	### 10.2 iOS Safari audio-unlock (locked requirement)
488	
489	- Web audio on iOS Safari is **suspended until a user gesture**. The AudioManager must **resume the audio context on the first tap** (Play button / first canvas tap) before playing music/SFX.
490	- Phaser's audio unlock helps, but we verify explicitly on iOS: no audio before first gesture, correct audio after.
491	- Mute state must survive the unlock (a muted player who taps Play stays muted).
492	
493	### 10.3 Browser support
494	
495	- Meet the matrix in §2.2. Primary QA on iOS Safari + Android Chrome.
496	- Graceful handling of blocked analytics (ad-blockers) — game fully playable with `gtag`/`fbq` absent (§7.1).
497	
498	### 10.4 Accessibility (basic, appropriate to an advergame)
499	
500	- Large, thumb-friendly tap targets; the whole canvas is the jump zone.
501	- Sufficient text/HUD contrast; hearts distinguishable by shape+fill, not color alone.
502	- Mute control always reachable.
503	- Full keyboard play on desktop (spacebar jump).
504	- No essential info conveyed by color alone.
505	- *(Full WCAG conformance is out of scope for a game canvas; this is a reasonable-effort baseline.)*
506	
507	### 10.5 Asset-size mindfulness
508	
509	- Stay within the download budget (§2.3): pack atlases tightly, compress audio, avoid oversized backgrounds (scale parallax art to max device resolution, not beyond).
510	- Lazy-load nothing critical to first play; everything needed for round 1 loads in Preload behind the bar.
511	- Prefer tint/shader variants over duplicate sheets (e.g. armored dog) to save bytes.
512	
513	---
514	
515	## 11. Open Questions / To Confirm With Client
516	
517	These block a *firm* cost/timeline. Each has a **spec'd sensible assumption** so work can proceed, but must be confirmed:
518	
519	| # | Open question | Assumption used in this spec |
520	|---|---|---|
521	| 1 | **Performance KPIs** — target load time & FPS on low-end phones | §2.3 budget (≤3 s TTI, 60 FPS / ≥30 FPS floor, ≤4–6 MB) |
522	| 2 | **Build timeline in weeks** | To be quoted; depends on art scope & these answers |
523	| 3 | **Final promo code + exact tabletki.ua landing URL** | Placeholder code; link to tabletki.ua root |
524	| 4 | **UI language & i18n** | Ukrainian primary; built i18n-ready (`i18n/strings.ts`) |
525	| 5 | **GA4 Measurement ID + Meta Pixel ID** | Injected via `VITE_*` env vars; needed before launch |
526	| 6 | **Brand assets** (logo, colors, product imagery) | Placeholders until brand kit provided |
527	| 7 | **Phase-2 5-breed select — committed?** | Deferred/roadmap only (§9); MVP = one dog |
528	| 8 | **Consent/CMP requirement** (GDPR) | Adapter consent-ready; banner UX TBD (§7.4) |
529	| 9 | **Orientation** (portrait vs landscape) & **CTA nav** (same/new tab on mobile) | Portrait-first; confirm CTA tab behavior |
530	| 10 | **Bush/puddle damage model** — damaging hazard vs harmless blocker | Treated as −1 HP hazard (§3.3) |
531	
532	---
533	
534	## 12. Estimate Framing
535	
536	The brief (§3A, §4) explicitly asks for **separate estimates for Code vs. Design/Animation**, plus a **weeks-long timeline** and a **min–max price**. This section structures the deliverables into two workstreams so they can feed the client's estimate. **Actual cost/timeline numbers depend on the open questions in §11** (especially art scope, perf KPIs, and whether phase 2 is committed) and are provided separately in the quote.
537	
538	### 12.1 Code workstream — deliverables
539	
540	**MVP:**
541	- Project scaffold (Phaser 3 + TS + Vite), static deploy pipeline (Cloudflare Pages / Netlify).
542	- Scene state machine (Boot/Preload/Menu/Game/Results).
543	- Auto-run + tap-to-jump; jump tuning.
544	- HP system (3 hearts, damage, invuln window, tablet heal cap).
545	- Scoring (tablets + survival).
546	- Spawner + difficulty curve (speed & density ramp).
547	- Entities: tick, tablet, bush/puddle, armor pickup (timed invulnerability logic).
548	- HUD (score, hearts, progress, pause, mute) + pause overlay.
549	- Victory/Game Over screens + promo-code CTA + tabletki.ua nav.
550	- AudioManager (SFX, music loop, mute persistence, **iOS audio-unlock**).
551	- `track()` analytics adapter → GA4 + Meta Pixel; the 3-event contract (§7).
552	- Object pooling / performance pass; browser-matrix QA.
553	- i18n-ready string layer.
554	
555	**Phase 2 (code):** dog-selection screen + choice persistence; duck/slide input verb + collision handling; combo/multiplier system + UI.
556	
557	### 12.2 Design / Animation workstream — deliverables
558	
559	**MVP:**
560	- **Hero dog** atlas: run, jump, damage, victory, defeat (5 states).
561	- **Park** environment: 1–2 parallax layers + ground tile (+ optional foreground).
562	- **Tick** (1), **tablet/product** (1), **bush/puddle** obstacles (1–2).
563	- **Armor** pickup + VFX (pickup burst, active aura, expiry tell).
564	- **UI kit & screens:** main menu, HUD, pause, Victory, Game Over; buttons, hearts, promo chip, icons.
565	- **Audio:** jump/hit/pickup SFX, victory/defeat stings, music loop.
566	
567	**Phase 2 (design):** 4 additional dog atlases (×5 states); dog-selection screen art; duck/slide obstacle art; combo/multiplier feedback art.
568	
569	### 12.3 Note on the two-workstream split
570	
571	The split is clean: the Code workstream can build against **placeholder art** (grey-box atlases with correct frame counts and dimensions) while the Design/Animation workstream produces finals in parallel, then assets swap in via the atlas pipeline (§8.4). This parallelism is what compresses the timeline — and it's why the final weeks/price figures in the quote hinge on confirming §11 (art scope + phase-2 commitment above all).
572

2	
3	**Document type:** Product & technical specification (buildable scope for estimate)
4	**Status:** Draft for client confirmation
5	**Source of requirements:** [`docs/2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md`](./2d-browser-runner-bi-brief.md) (client cost-estimation brief, English translation)
6	**Date:** 2026-07-23
7	
8	> **How to read this document.** The client brief is the source of *requirements*. A product interview then locked a set of *decisions* that resolve the brief's open ambiguities (e.g. endless vs. finite, MVP vs. phase 2). Where a locked decision narrows or overrides the brief, this spec follows the decision and says so. Section 11 lists what still needs client confirmation before a firm cost/timeline can be committed.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Overview & Goals
13	
14	### 1.1 What we are building
15	
16	A **mobile-first, branded 2D browser runner** that promotes a dog flea-and-tick tablet. The player controls a hero dog that auto-runs through a park, jumps over obstacles, avoids **ticks**, and collects **tablets**. The round is a **finite single level (~60–90 s)** ending in **Victory** (reach the finish line) or **Game Over** (lose all health). After the round, a single call-to-action surfaces a **promo code** and links to **[tabletki.ua](http://tabletki.ua)** to buy the product.
17	
18	This is an advergame: the gameplay is the vehicle, and the marketing outcomes are the point.
19	
20	### 1.2 Marketing objective
21	
22	Per the brief (§1), two goals:
23	
24	1. **Awareness** — teach, through play, that ticks are a threat and the tablet is the protection. The "tablet as armor" power-up (§3.7) makes the product mechanic *be* the protection.
25	2. **Conversion** — drive tablet purchase via the post-round CTA to tabletki.ua (brief §3, "CTA button").
26	
27	### 1.3 Audience
28	
29	Dog owners on **mobile web**, reached through paid social / display where Meta Pixel and GA4 attribution matter. Casual players; sessions are short and one-handed. UI language assumed **Ukrainian primary**, built i18n-ready (see §11).
30	
31	### 1.4 Success signals (tied to the three analytics events)
32	
33	The entire funnel is observable through three events (full contract in §7):
34	
35	| Funnel stage | Signal | Event |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Engagement | Player starts a round | `start_game` |
38	| Completion & quality | Player finishes (win or lose), with score & duration | `finish_game` (`result`, `score`, `duration_s`) |
39	| **Conversion** | Player taps the buy CTA | `click_buy` (`destination`, `promo_code`) |
40	
41	Primary KPI is `click_buy / start_game` (intent-to-purchase rate). `finish_game` with `result=win` vs. `lose` and `duration_s` tells us whether difficulty is tuned so players actually reach the CTA.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 2. Platforms & Performance Targets
46	
47	### 2.1 Platform priority
48	
49	**Mobile web first**, desktop supported (brief §2). Touch is the primary input; desktop uses tap/click and spacebar.
50	
51	### 2.2 Supported browser matrix
52	
53	| Tier | Browser / OS | Support level |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| Primary | iOS Safari (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
56	| Primary | Android Chrome (last 2 major versions) | Fully supported, primary QA target |
57	| Secondary | Desktop Chrome / Edge / Firefox (current) | Fully supported |
58	| Secondary | Desktop Safari (current) | Fully supported |
59	| Best-effort | Samsung Internet, mobile Firefox | Should work; not a QA gate |

62	
63	Because the brief sets no numbers, we propose these targets. They drive art budgets and QA gates and must be confirmed:
64	
65	| Metric | Target | Notes |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Frame rate | 60 FPS on mid-range phones; **≥30 FPS floor** on low-end (≈2–3-year-old Android) | Gameplay must never dip below the floor |
68	| Time-to-interactive (first load, warm CDN) | **≤3 s** on a 4G connection | Menu interactive |

70	| Input latency (tap → jump) | ≤1 frame of processing | Tap responsiveness is the whole game |

76	
77	## 3. Gameplay Design
78	
79	### 3.1 Core loop
80	
81	```
82	auto-run forward  →  read upcoming hazard  →  tap to jump  →  land / collect / take hit
83	      ↑                                                                    │
84	      └──────────────────── repeat until finish line or 0 HP ──────────────┘

317	## 7. Analytics & Tracking Spec
318	
319	### 7.1 Adapter design
320	
321	A **thin `track(event, params)` adapter** is the single choke point for all analytics. Game code never calls `gtag`/`fbq` directly — it calls `track()`, which fans out to **GA4 (gtag)** and **Meta Pixel (fbq)**.
322	
323	```ts
324	type AnalyticsEvent = 'start_game' | 'finish_game' | 'click_buy';
325	
326	function track(event: AnalyticsEvent, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
327	  // GA4
328	  window.gtag?.('event', event, params);
329	  // Meta Pixel — custom events via trackCustom
330	  window.fbq?.('trackCustom', event, params);
331	  // Dev/QA: console mirror when a debug flag is on
332	  if (DEBUG_ANALYTICS) console.debug('[track]', event, params);
333	}
334	```
335	
336	Rationale:
337	- **One contract, two sinks.** Adding/removing a sink (or a consent gate) is a one-file change.
338	- **Safe if a pixel is absent.** Optional chaining means a missing/blocked `gtag`/`fbq` never throws (ad-blockers are common on the audience).
339	- **Testable.** Event emission can be asserted in isolation.
340	
341	### 7.2 Event / parameter contract
342	
343	#### `start_game` — a round begins
344	
345	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
346	|---|---|---|---|---|
347	| *(none required)* | — | — | — | Fired once when the Play scene starts the run |
348	
349	#### `finish_game` — fires on BOTH Victory and Game Over
350	
351	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
352	|---|---|---|---|---|
353	| `result` | `'win' \| 'lose'` | ✅ | `'win'` | `win` = reached finish; `lose` = 0 HP |
354	| `score` | integer | ✅ | `1450` | Final score at round end |
355	| `duration_s` | integer (seconds) | ✅ | `72` | Wall-clock round length, start → end |
356	
357	#### `click_buy` — CTA tapped on results screen
358	
359	| Param | Type | Required | Example | Notes |
360	|---|---|---|---|---|
361	| `destination` | string | ✅ | `'tabletki.ua'` | Fixed for MVP |
362	| `promo_code` | string | ✅ | `'DOG10'` | The code shown on the CTA (see §11) |
363	
364	> All three event **names** are fixed by the brief (§3B: `start_game`, `finish_game`, `click_buy`) — do not rename.
365	
366	### 7.3 GA4 (gtag) + Meta Pixel (fbq) wiring
367	
368	- Both snippets load in `index.html` `<head>` (standard install), parameterized by **GA4 Measurement ID** and **Meta Pixel ID** (see §11 — needed before launch).
369	- IDs injected via Vite env vars (`VITE_GA4_ID`, `VITE_FB_PIXEL_ID`) so staging/prod differ without code edits.
370	- GA4 receives events via `gtag('event', …)`; Meta Pixel via `fbq('trackCustom', …)`. (Meta standard events like `Purchase` are **not** used — the brief's three custom names take priority; a `Purchase` mapping can be added later if the client wants Ads Manager optimization on it.)
371	
372	### 7.4 Consent / GDPR note
373	
374	- The audience is EU-adjacent (Ukraine); ad pixels imply personal-data processing.
375	- **Recommendation:** a lightweight consent gate. `track()` is the natural enforcement point — buffer or drop events until consent is granted, and only initialize `fbq`/`gtag` post-consent (Consent Mode v2 for GA4).
376	- Exact consent UX / whether a CMP is required depends on the client's legal stance — **flag in §11.** MVP ships the adapter consent-ready even if the banner is deferred.
